title: The Tale of the Fourth Brother, the One-Eyed Butcher

paragraphs.en: My fourth brother, the one-eyed butcher in Baghdad, prospered by selling meat to the wealthy. For several years, he accumulated wealth and property. One day, an old man with a long beard entered his shop, paid for meat, and left.
paragraphs.zh: 我的四弟，巴格达的那个独眼屠夫，在给富人卖肉的生意中发了财。几年下来，他积累了相当可观的财富和产业。一天，一位留着长胡子的老者走进他的店铺，买了一些肉便离开了。

paragraphs.en: Intrigued by the gleaming silver coins, my brother saved them separately. The old man returned every month for five months, each time leaving more white coins that my brother carefully stored away.
paragraphs.zh: 被那些闪闪发光的银币吸引，哥哥将它们单独保存起来。那位老人连续五个月每月都来一次，每次留下更多的白花花的银币，哥哥小心翼翼地把它们收了起来。

paragraphs.en: One day, the butcher tried to take out money from his chest to buy sheep but found only round paper inside. He cried out in frustration, drawing a crowd who heard his story. Rising, he slaughtered a ram as usual, hung it up in his shop, and cut some meat to hang outside, hoping the old man would return.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，屠夫想从柜子里取出钱去买羊，却发现里面只有些圆形的纸片。他气愤地喊了出来，引来了一群人听他的讲述。随后，他像往常一样宰了一只山羊，挂在店门口，并切了些肉挂在外面，希望能吸引那位老人回来。

paragraphs.en: Soon, the old man appeared with money in hand. The butcher caught him, shouting, "O Muslims, come and hear what this crooked old man did to me!" When questioned by the old man, he asked, "What do you prefer: to let go or expose me?"
paragraphs.zh: 不久，那老人带着钱出现了。屠夫一把抓住他，喊道：“穆斯林们，快来听听这个狡猾的老头对我做了什么！”面对老人的质问，屠夫脱口而出：“您是愿意放了我，还是想让我曝光？”

paragraphs.en: The old man replied, "For selling human flesh as mutton." The brother denied it, but the old man cried out that a man was hanging in his shop. The brother admitted his property and life were forfeit if true.
paragraphs.zh: 老人回答说：“是因为他把人肉卖成了羊肉。”兄弟否认此事，但老人喊道，有个男人正悬挂在他的店铺里。兄弟承认如果属实，他的财产和生命都将不保。

paragraphs.en: The people rushed into the shop and found a man's carcass instead of the ram. They seized the butcher, calling him an infidel and villain. Even his friends turned against him, saying he had given them human flesh to eat.
paragraphs.zh: 人们蜂拥而入，却发现摊上是一具人的尸体而不是羊。他们一把抓住屠夫，骂他异教徒和恶棍。就连他的朋友也反过来指责他，说他给他们吃了人肉。

paragraphs.en: The old man struck out his eye, leaving him blind in one eye.
paragraphs.zh: 老人瞎了一只眼，从此成了独眼屠夫。

paragraphs.en: They took the butcher to the chief of police, who believed the old man's accusations. The brother tried to explain but was flogged nearly five hundred times and lost everything—his money, property, sheep, and shop. He was paraded through the city for three days before being banished.
paragraphs.zh: 他们将屠夫带到了警察局长那里，局长相信了老人的指控。兄弟试图解释，却挨了近五百鞭打，失去了所有财产——钱、房产、羊和店铺。他被在城里游街示众三天后，最终被驱逐出境。

paragraphs.en: My brother traveled to a large city and opened a cobbler's shop. One day, while out on business, he witnessed the king preparing for a hunt. The king noticed my brother’s one-eyed appearance and rode away with his entourage.
paragraphs.zh: 我的哥哥前往一个大城市开设了一家修鞋店。一天，他外出办事时目睹了国王准备狩猎的情景。国王注意到了我哥哥独眼的特征，随后便带着随从扬长而去。

paragraphs.en: My brother was then beaten by the king’s attendants without explanation. He sought help from a servant in the royal household, who revealed that the king despised one-eyed men and intended to kill him.
paragraphs.zh: 我的哥哥随后被国王的侍从无故毒打。他向宫中一名仆人求援，那人透露说，国王厌恶独眼人，并打算将他置于死地。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused her tale. Dinarzad remarked, "What an intriguing story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night when I have more to share if you spare me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的讲述。丁纳札德remarked道：“真是引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹adapted回答道：“如果你能让我活到明天晚上，我还有很多精彩的内容要与你分享。”

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Shahrazad began again:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹又开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the tailor told the king of China that the barber had relayed a message from his guests to the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 我听见，幸福的国王啊，裁缝曾向中国国王禀报，理发师转述了他客人的口信给哈里发。

paragraphs.en: My brother fled from the city to avoid recognition and settled in another town where he prospered. One day, while enjoying himself, he heard horse hooves behind him. He cried, "The judgment of God is upon me," and sought shelter but found only a closed door that opened when pushed.
paragraphs.zh: 我的兄弟逃离了城市，以避免被人认出，便在另一个镇上安顿下来，生活颇为顺利。有一天，他正悠然自得时，突然听到身后有马蹄声。他脱口而出：“天谴临头了。”于是寻找避身之处，却只找到一扇紧闭的门，推开门后却发现门自动开了。

paragraphs.en: Two men seized him, accusing him of tormenting them for three nights by plotting to kill their master and making them suffer. They searched him and found a knife in his belt.
paragraphs.zh: 两个男人抓住他，指控他在三个晚上密谋杀害他们的主人，并让他们饱受折磨。他们在他的腰带上搜出了一把刀。

paragraphs.en: My brother pleaded with them, "Please listen to my story; I have a strange tale." But they ignored him, beating him and stripping him naked. Finding old scars on his back, they declared him cursed.
paragraphs.zh: 我的兄弟恳求他们说：“请听我讲述我的故事，我有一个奇怪的故事。”但他们置之不理，拳打脚踢，并将他剥得赤条条的。他们在他的背部发现了旧伤痕，于是断定他是被诅咒的人。

paragraphs.en: The chief of police was called, and my brother feared for his life. He begged the chief to hear his story before condemning him.
paragraphs.zh: 警察局长被叫了过来，我的哥哥生怕自己性命不保。他央求警察局长听一听他的解释再做定论。

paragraphs.en: The chief saw the scars and said, "You must have committed a grave crime." He sentenced my brother to a hundred lashes and paraded him through the city as a warning. The chief then banished him from the town.
paragraphs.zh: 首领看到伤疤，说道：“你肯定犯下了严重的罪行。”他下令将我哥哥鞭打一百，并在全城游街示众。随后，首领将他逐出了城镇。

paragraphs.en: I found my brother wandering and learned his tale. I secretly brought him back to Baghdad and provided for him.
paragraphs.zh: 我发现哥哥四处游荡，并听他讲述了这段经历。我暗中将他带回巴格达，照顾起他来。

paragraphs.en: My brother's escape, capture, trial, and exile were harrowing experiences that led me to take him in with generosity.
paragraphs.zh: 我兄弟的逃亡、被捕、受审和流放的经历令人痛心，促使我以宽宏大量的态度接纳了他。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued her tale the next night. "O Happy King," she began, "the tailor recounted to the Chinese king what the barber had shared with his guests about the caliph."
paragraphs.zh: 沙海拉扎德在第二天晚上继续讲述她的故事：“哦，幸福的国王，裁缝向中国国王讲述了理发师与客人分享的关于哈里发的事情。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph laughed so hard he fell back and ordered a gift for Shahrazad. But she replied, "By God, my lord, though I am not verbose, I must complete the stories of my other brothers. This way, our lord will know all their tales, have them recorded, and understand that I am not a talkative man."
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发笑得前仰后合，差点摔倒，并吩咐为沙赫拉兹阿德准备一份礼物。但她回答说：“主上啊，虽然我并不啰唆，但我必须讲完其他兄弟的故事。这样，主上才能了解他们各自的故事，将它们记录下来，并明白我不是一个爱说话的人。”

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad then said to her sister, "What an intriguing story!" Shahrazad responded with confidence, "Wait until tomorrow night if I live; you'll hear one even more captivating."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。迪纳兹达对她说：“真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹达自信地回应道：“如果我能活到明天晚上，你就会听到一个更加扣人心弦的故事。”
